source1: Halil Inalcik, The Caliphate and Ataturk's Inkilabs, Belleten XLVI (Turk Tarih Kurumu) - https://belleten.gov.tr/tam-metin-pdf/1733/eng
source2: Cezmi Eraslan, Abolishment of the Caliphate and Turkey's Transformation to Modern State, Ataturk Arastirma Merkezi Dergisi 17(50), 2001 - https://dergipark.org.tr/en/pub/aamd/article/759225
notes: Ankara GNA elite were Muslims: abolished the sultanate 1922 but elected Abdulmecid caliph, Kemal argued in Islamic terms; caliphate abolished 1924, secularization followed. Ruling group coded Islam at conquest, hence same tradition.

source1: John F. Hansman, Elymais, Encyclopaedia Iranica VIII/4, 1998 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elymais
source2: Josef Wiesehofer, Ardasir I i. History, Encyclopaedia Iranica II/4, 1986 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ardasir-i
notes: Hansman: Elymaeans worshipped Semitic gods of Babylon/Assyria (Bel, Nanaia), possibly syncretized with Elamite deities; Ardashir ended Elymais c.221. Wiesehofer: Ardashir professed Mazda-worship; Sasanians kept Zoroastrianism. Middle Persian coins and inscriptions.

source1: C. E. Bosworth, Ghurids, Encyclopaedia Iranica X/6, 2001 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ghurids
source2: Farhad Daftary and Azim Nanji, Ismaili Communities - South Asia, Institute of Ismaili Studies (from Encyclopedia of Modern Asia), 2002 - https://www.iis.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/ismailis_south_asia-142506347.pdf
notes: Ghurids were staunch Sunnis; Mu'izz al-Din forced the Sumras of Lower Sind to accept suzerainty 1182 (Bosworth). Population largely Hindu with Ismaili converts under Sumra protection; exact composition undocumented. Ghurids stayed Sunni, Persian-literate.

Selim I defeated the Mamluks 1516-17 and took Egypt. Both ruling groups Sunni Muslim: Mamluks patrons of Sunni al-Azhar and 'champions of Islam'; Ottomans Sunni against Safavid Shiism, received keys of Mecca.

source1: Matteo G. Randazzo, Nikephoros Phokas and the Byzantine Reconquista of the Islamic Emirate of Crete (961 AD): An Alternative View, Imago Temporis. Medium Aevum XVIII, 2024 - https://raco.cat/index.php/ImagoTemporis/article/download/427634/522121/628940
notes: Orthodox Byzantines reconquered Crete 961. Randazzo: rural bulk of population stayed Christian, Islamization limited to the capital. Older scholarship (Christides) posits a Muslim majority, so A is disputed; if A were Islam, adopted would be N.

source1: Francois Vallat, Elam vi. Elamite religion, Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-vi
source2: Francois Vallat, Elam i. The history of Elam, Encyclopaedia Iranica VIII/3, 1998 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-i
notes: Shutruk-Nahhunte and Kutir-Nahhunte ended the Kassite dynasty c.1155 BCE, carrying Mesopotamian monuments to Susa. Vallat: elamization of the pantheon progressed under the Shutrukids; Shilhak-Inshushinak's stele lists one Mesopotamian god; Elamite inscriptions dominate.

source1: Muazzam Hussain Khan, Danauja Rai, Raja, Banglapedia (Asiatic Society of Bangladesh) - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Danauja_Rai,_Raja
source2: M. Harunur Rashid, Deva Dynasty, Banglapedia (Asiatic Society of Bangladesh) - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Deva_Dynasty
notes: This is the later Vaishnava Deva dynasty: Danauja Rai (Dasharathadeva) promoted Vaishnavism to predominance. Database Buddhism likely reflects the earlier 8th-9th c. Buddhist Devas. Muslim attack 1302 ended Hindu rule at Sonargaon; conquerors stayed Muslim.

source1: Charles Melville and Abbas Zaryab, Chobanids, Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/chobanids
source2: Charles Melville, Coban, Encyclopaedia Iranica V/8, 1992 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/coban
notes: Il-khanid court Islamized after Ghazan's conversion (Amitai, Iranica). Chobanid founder Coban was 'a pious and sincere Muslim' (Melville); Chobanids ruled through puppet Hulegid khans 1335-57. Both ruling groups Muslim.

source1: Tilman Nagel, Buyids, Encyclopaedia Iranica IV/6, 1990 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/buyids
notes: Buyids were Shi'ite Iranian amirs (Nagel); Toghril Beg, allied with orthodox Muslims and the Abbasid caliph, entered Baghdad 1055; Fars fell to Shabankara Kurds, then Seljuks, c.1062. Shi'a versus Sunni counts as same tradition.

source1: Rachel Sponzo, Tigrinya, Encyclopedia of World Cultures Supplement (Gale), via Encyclopedia.com - https://encyclopedia.com/places/africa/eritrea-political-geography/tigrinya
notes: Medri Bahri's highland Tigrinya core was mainly Orthodox Christian (Sponzo: most Tigrinya Orthodox, about 7% Muslim); Islam mostly coastal, so A coded Christianity. Conquering Kingdom of Italy was Catholic; Ethiopian interlude also Christian. Same tradition.
